newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: LatAm stocks seen higher amid earnings, Carnival.
newsitem.headline: LatAm stocks seen higher amid earnings, Carnival.

text.p: Latin American bolsas were expected to be upbeat during Carnival week, with most stocks driven higher by a good reporting season, dealers said.
The markets of Brazil and Venezuela will be closed Monday and Tuesday for Carnival celebrations, while Chile's bolsa was expected to grab the spotlight at the start of the week.
Chilean stocks surged 3.8 percent Friday on news of the Central Bank's surprise decision Thursday to trim interest rates, halting its year-long policy of tight credit.
Investors had not expected the bank to cut rates before March, and were completely caught off guard.
The bolsa, however, was likely to pause for breath mid-week as players start cashing in their gains, said Jaime Pea y Lillo, a portfolio analyst at brokerage Socimer.

"We will see profit-taking tomorrow or the day after. A lot of shares have risen fast in a short space of time," said Pea y Lillo. He also predicted investors would soon focus again on fourth quarter earnings.
The 40-share index rallied 4.8 percent last week to 115.89 points.
Brazil's Bovespa index also shot up 4.4 percent last week and was seen firming.

Players were expected to track Telebras ahead of next Monday's options expiration in a week shortened by Carnival. Telebras preferred, the underlying stock on most options, closed Friday at 93.30 reais, raising the odds that the 92 real strike price could be exercised.
Players with long positions looked victorious, but traders warned volatility could rise before the settlement deadline.
Brazilian bolsas reopen Wednesday at 1300 local time/1500 GMT for a half-day session.
In Argentina the bolsa was seen keeping a positive bias.

"The market's momentum will probably last in the short run," said trader Carlos Quarracino at Banco Crdito Provincial. "This week players will be choosy and focused on company results, which so far have bolstered good economic forecasts."
The bolsa's upward march could be reined in somewhat by next week's options expirations.
"Settlements will probably be heavy and many people might sell immediately afterwards, causing a jump in supply," said Norman Trabucco at Zaracan traders.
The blue-chip MerVal index pierced 700 for the first time in three years last week, gaining 1.5 percent to close Friday at 701.8.
Mexican stocks were seen little traded and volatile this week. Last week, they soaked up profit-taking and still managed to edge up 0.2 percent to 3654.34 on the leading index.
Traders said stocks were consolidating between 3600-3700 and would be conditioned by company results.
Electioneering for municipal elections and the Treasury bill auction were also seen as factors this week.
((-- Buenos Aires Newsroom 541 318-0657))
